newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says February inflation 16.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says February inflation 16.7 pct.

text.p: Sri Lanka's February inflation, based on a 12-month moving average, rose to 16.7 percent from 16.4 percent in January, the Census and Statistics Department said on Friday.
The inflation rate rose mainly because of increases in the prices of tea dust, beef, some varieties of fresh and dried fish and some of vegetables, it said in a statement.
The Colombo Consumers' Price Index (CCPI) for February fell to 2,031.3, a drop of 11.4 index points or 0.6 percent from January's 2,042.7, it added.
The decrease in the CCPI index was mainly because of a fall in prices of rice, sugar, dried chillies, onions, limes, coconuts, potatoes and some varieties of dried fish fell, it said.
